issues.legal_issue: A personal land grant burdened with religious service is not covered by the statutory power to resume grants made for the performance of religious charity or service.
material_facts: The grant comprised both warams and was found to be personal to the grantees, rather than an emolument for holding a service office.
The grantees were required to perform service for the temples, but the grant also contained a personal element for their benefit.
After the grantees alienated part of the land and stopped performing the service, revenue authorities ordered resumption and regrant of the land to the temples under the Act.
The alienees challenged the revenue authorities’ jurisdiction to resume the grant under that provision.
issues.conclusion: The personal inam burdened with service did not fall within section 44-B; the revenue authorities could not resume and regrant it under that section. Such inams remained governed by Board’s Standing Order 54, class (b), and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 44-B(1) of the Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act, 1927, read with sections 44-B(2)(a)(iii), 44-B(2)(f)(i) and (ii), applies to inams granted directly to a temple, service inams, and inams whose whole income is intended for charity, not personal inams merely burdened with service. The structure of the resumption and regrant provisions supports that construction. A personal grant burdened with service is distinct from a service grant; whether the former is resumable for failure to perform service depends on whether the circumstances of the grant made it conditional on performance. The Court referred to Shrimant Lakhamgouda Basavprabhu Sardesai v. Raosaheb Baswantrao and to Board’s Standing Order 54, class (b), as amended.

predicates.challenge_to_public_resumption: A party challenged the authority of public officials to resume and regrant land under a power concerning religious or charitable grants.
predicates.personal_grant_with_service_burden: The land was granted personally to an individual, who was also required to perform service for a religious institution.
predicates.grant_included_personal_benefit: The grant was not wholly intended as income for the religious institution or as emoluments for performing its service.

issues.definition: When a challenge to public resumption concerns a personal grant that required religious service but included a personal benefit, the resumption power does not authorize resumption of the grant.
